question: On a multi-lane roadway posted at 35 mph, may the single-lane regulatory-sign size be used, and what size must a STOP sign still use?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. Under the MUTCD's general dimensioning rule, the reduced "Minimum" sign sizes may only be used on low-speed roadways with operating speeds of 30 mph or less; a multi-lane roadway posted at 35 mph does not qualify, so the smaller (minimum/single-lane-minimum) sizes may not be used and the full prescribed (Conventional Road) dimensions apply. However, the specific numeric dimensions for the STOP (R1-1) sign itself (Table 2B-1) are not included in the evidence provided, so I cannot state the exact STOP sign size — only that it must be no smaller than the prescribed Conventional Road size for that context. Standards (mandatory): - "The sign dimensions prescribed in the sign size tables in the various Parts and Chapters in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05) shall be used unless engineering judgment determines that other sizes are appropriate in accordance with the following." - "The sizes shown in the Minimum columns that are smaller than the sizes shown in the Conventional Road columns in the various sign size tables in this Manual shall only be used on low-speed roadways, alleys, site roadways open to public travel, and on low-volume rural roads with operating speeds of 30 mph or less; and only where the reduced legend size would be adequate for the regulation or warning or where physical conditions preclude the use of larger sizes." — A 35-mph multi-lane roadway exceeds this 30-mph threshold, so reduced sizes are not permitted. - Note 3 to the school-area sign size table states that minimum sign sizes for multi-lane conventional roads shall be as shown in the Conventional Road column (i.e., the smaller Minimum column values cannot be used on multi-lane roads). Guidance (recommended): - For school-area signs, "The sizes in the Oversized column should be used on roadways that have four or more lanes with posted speed limits of 40 mph or higher" — showing that larger, not smaller, sizes are the recommended direction on higher-speed multi-lane roads. - For guide-sign lettering, Table 2D-2 distinguishes Single-Lane and Multi-Lane columns by speed range; on multi-lane roads in the 30–40 mph range, the larger Multi-Lane column values apply rather than the Single-Lane values. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2D-2 (Sheet 1, Post-Mounted Signs) shows separate Single-Lane and Multi-Lane letter/numeral size columns, with the Multi-Lane 30–40 mph column generally requiring larger sizes than the Single-Lane column for the same speed range. - [Image 2] Table 7B-1 lists Conventional Road, Minimum, and Oversized sizes for school-area regulatory signs, and its Note 3 states that minimum sign sizes for multi-lane conventional roads shall be as shown in the Conventional Road column. - [Image 3] Shows the Section 2A.07 Standard text restricting Minimum-column sizes to low-speed roadways with operating speeds of 30 mph or less. Insufficient evidence note: The regulatory sign size table containing the STOP (R1-1) sign dimensions (e.g., Table 2B-1) is not among the evidence supplied, so the exact required STOP sign dimension (in inches) for a multi-lane 35-mph roadway cannot be quoted from this evidence. Citations: - Section 2A.07 Standard §2 (p.45) - Section 7B.01 Guidance §3 (p.972) - Section 2D.07 Guidance §5 (p.210) - Table 2D-2 (p.210) - Table 7B-1 (p.971)
gold_answer: For regulatory signs other than STOP, the single-lane size may be used at 35 mph or less. The STOP-sign exception remains: the multi-lane STOP size is 36 x 36 inches.
